newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds stable in lackluster activity.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds stable in lackluster activity.

text.p: Argentine bonds finished flat Monday after a session of dull, cautious trading.
"There was very little trade and it was cautious," said a trader at a foreign bank.
The dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 was flat at 125.29, while the FRB Brady bond due 2005 was also stable at 88-3/4.
The market was down early in the session but according to traders it found technical support when the FRB hit 88-1/2.
Another trader said he "was not convinced that the profit-taking is over," referring to the slump Friday that set in after the near unbroken ascent in prices during January.

Traders said the market was keeping a close watch on the U.S. Treasuries market where the 30-year yield rose five basis points to 6.93 percent. Some see the 7.0 percent level as a key point at which a larger bout of profit-taking could hit Latin American markets.
In the money markets, call money rates fell to 5.35 percent from 5.50 percent.
